chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
The witr is three rak'ahs: two separated, and one.

key_terms.الْوِتْرُ: the witr prayer, the concluding odd-numbered prayer of the night prayer
key_terms.ثَلَاثُ: three, indicating the total number of rak'ahs mentioned here
key_terms.ثِنْتَيْنِ: two units, referring to the shaf' portion
key_terms.مَفْصُولَةً: separated, meaning performed distinctly rather than joined
key_terms.وَوَاحِدَةً: and one, referring to the final single rak'ah of witr

ai.seo_question: How should the witr prayer be performed according to Imam Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal form of witr as three rak'ahs performed in a separated manner: two rak'ahs apart from one rak'ah. It supports the ruling that the two rak'ahs of shaf' and the one rak'ah of witr are not to be joined as a continuous three-rak'ah prayer.
